settings.label: Site
settings.description: Address, appearance, menu and redirects of the public site.

page.title: Site
page.description: The public site shows the pages that plugins publish (blog, shop, catalog).
page.noPages: No plugin publishes pages yet. Install a blog or shop plugin so the site has content.

address.title: Address
address.description: Where the site answers. The app stays at the path set in General.
address.hostHint: Use it when the site has its own domain, such as www.yourcompany.com, pointed at this server. Empty, the site uses the same address as the app.
address.pathHint: Empty = root. Without its own domain, it must differ from the app path.
address.locked: Only system administrators can change the address.
address.indexing: Let search engines find the site
address.indexingHint: When off, the site stays open to anyone with the link but asks search engines (Google, Bing) not to list it and does not publish the sitemap. Useful while the site is being built.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: Theme and presentation used on every page.
appearance.themeHint: Themes come from plugins. The default theme is simple and follows dark mode.
appearance.taglineHint: Shown below the company name at the top of the site. Up to 160 characters. Name, logo and color come from Settings → Organization.

menu.title: Menu
menu.description: Drag to change the order. Hidden items stay online; they only leave the menu.

redirects.title: Moved addresses
redirects.description: When the address of some content changes (for example a post slug), the old address leads to the new one. Remove a redirect if the old address should answer "page not found" again.
redirects.empty: No address has moved so far.

cache.title: Page updates
cache.description: Pages are kept so they open fast and refresh on their own when the content changes. Use the button if something stays out of date.
cache.purged: Pages will be generated again on the next visit

errors.path: Use only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, in a single segment (e.g. blog).
errors.pathReserved: This path is used by the API. Choose another one.
errors.host: Enter only the domain, such as www.yourcompany.com, without http:// or a path.
errors.pathTaken: The app already uses this path. Choose another one or set a domain for the site.
errors.redirectSource: Start with / and do not use spaces, ? or #.
errors.redirectTarget: Use a site path (/blog) or an address starting with https://.

customers.title: Customer accounts
customers.description: Visitors create an account on the site itself to follow orders and whatever plugins offer. Accounts are separate from app users.
customers.enableHint: Shows "Sign in" at the top of the site and the account pages (sign in, sign up, password reset).
customers.required: On because an installed plugin has customer pages.
customers.empty: No customer has signed up yet.
customers.linkPeopleHint: When the customer confirms the email, the account is linked to the person with the same email. If there is none, a new contact is created for the owner below.
customers.ownerHint: Without an owner, the site only links customers to people that already exist.

languages.title: Languages
languages.description: The site opens in {{language}}, the organization language. Other languages get their own address.
languages.hint: Plugins show translated content when the record has a version in that language (for example a title_en field). Without a translation, the original text appears. Account pages and theme texts come in Portuguese or English.

pathRedirects.title: Redirects
pathRedirects.description: Send visitors of an old address to a site page or to another website. Useful when replacing a website: old links keep working. A site page that answers the old address takes precedence.
pathRedirects.sourceHint: Path after the site address, starting with /.
pathRedirects.targetHint: A site path (/blog) or a full address (https://…).
pathRedirects.permanentHint: Tells search engines to replace the old address with the new one. Turn off for promotions and short-lived changes.
